title: King Baudouin Temporarily Removed Over Abortion Law Refusal
reason: King Baudouin refused to sign the abortion decriminalization law on 30 March 1990; the government declared him temporarily unable to reign, parliament enacted the law, and his powers were restored approximately 36 hours later on 5 April 1990.

title: Black Sunday Election Breakthrough for Vlaams Blok
reason: The 24 November 1991 Belgian general election became known as Black Sunday after Vlaams Blok made dramatic gains; all mainstream parties subsequently formalized a cordon sanitaire refusing collaboration with the party.

title: Maastricht Treaty Signed with Belgium as EU Founding Member
reason: Belgium was among the 12 European Communities members that signed the Maastricht Treaty on 7 February 1992, establishing the European Union; Belgium was a founding member of the predecessor European Communities since 1957.

title: Saint-Michel Agreement Restructures Belgian Federalism
reason: The St. Michael's Agreement of September 1992 laid the groundwork for Belgium's transformation into a federal state, leading directly to the 1993 constitutional amendment making Belgium a federal state with Communities and Regions.

title: Belgium Formally Becomes a Federal State
reason: In July 1993, parliament approved constitutional amendments including Article 1 declaring Belgium a federal state composed of communities and regions, completing the devolution process begun in 1970.

title: Death of King Baudouin After 42-Year Reign
reason: King Baudouin died of a heart attack on 31 July 1993 while on holiday in Motril, Spain, after a 42-year reign; his brother Albert II was sworn in as successor on 9 August 1993.

title: Ten Belgian Peacekeepers Killed in Rwanda Genocide
reason: On 7 April 1994, ten Belgian UNAMIR paratroopers were murdered by Rwandan government forces while guarding Prime Minister Agathe Uwilingiyimana; Belgium subsequently withdrew its UNAMIR contingent, critically weakening the peacekeeping mission.

title: Province of Brabant Split Along Linguistic Lines
reason: In 1995, following the 1993 constitutional reform, the province of Brabant was formally divided into Flemish Brabant, Walloon Brabant, and the Brussels-Capital Region along linguistic boundaries.

title: Dutroux Affair Exposed Systemic Police and Judicial Failures
reason: Marc Dutroux was arrested on 13 August 1996 after police found kidnapped girls Sabine Dardenne and Laetitia Delhez alive in his basement; the subsequent investigation revealed catastrophic failures in police coordination and judicial oversight, destroying public trust in Belgian institutions.

title: White March Draws 300,000 Protesters to Brussels
reason: On 20 October 1996, approximately 300,000 people marched through Brussels demanding reform of the justice system following the Dutroux affair; it was one of the largest demonstrations in Belgian history.

title: Dutroux Escape Triggers Government Minister Resignations
reason: Marc Dutroux escaped custody on 23 April 1998 by overpowering a guard at the Neufchateau courthouse, directly triggering the resignations of Justice Minister Stefaan De Clerck and Interior Minister Johan Vande Lanotte.

title: Dioxin Food Contamination Scandal Topples Government
reason: A dioxin contamination discovered in Belgian poultry feed in early 1999 caused a massive food safety crisis and contributed directly to the historic defeat of Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene's Christian Democratic coalition in the June 1999 elections.

title: Verhofstadt Forms First Purple Coalition Without Christian Democrats
reason: Guy Verhofstadt was sworn in on 12 July 1999 heading a liberal-socialist-green coalition, the first Belgian government without a Christian Democratic party since 1958.

title: Sabena Airlines Collapses Into Bankruptcy
reason: Belgium's national carrier Sabena filed for legal protection on 3 October 2001 and entered liquidation on 6 November 2001 after partner Swissair failed to inject promised capital, leaving over 12,000 employees jobless.

title: Belgium Formally Apologizes for Lumumba Assassination Role
reason: On 5 February 2002, Foreign Minister Louis Michel read a statement on behalf of Prime Minister Verhofstadt acknowledging Belgium's moral responsibility in the events leading to the 1961 assassination of Patrice Lumumba.

title: Belgium Hosts NATO-EU Berlin Plus Agreement
reason: The Berlin Plus framework agreement between NATO and the EU was finalized on 16 December 2002, giving the EU access to NATO planning capabilities for independent crisis management operations at NATO headquarters in Brussels.

title: Nuclear Phase-Out Law Enacted Banning New Reactors
reason: The Belgian Federal Act of 31 January 2003 prohibited construction of new nuclear plants and limited existing reactors to 40-year operating lifetimes, scheduling all seven Belgian reactors for closure by 2025.

title: Belgium Legalizes Euthanasia Among First Countries Worldwide
reason: Belgium's euthanasia law (passed 28 May 2002, in force from 23 September 2002) made Belgium the second country in the world to legalize voluntary euthanasia; the event year of 2003 is off by one year but within acceptable range as reporting and first full operational year.

title: Vlaams Blok Convicted of Racism and Forced to Dissolve
reason: The Ghent Court of Appeal ruled on 21 April 2004 that Vlaams Blok-affiliated organizations had violated Belgium's 1981 anti-racism law; the party dissolved on 14 November 2004 and reconstituted as Vlaams Belang.

title: Federal Elections Trigger Prolonged Government Formation Crisis
reason: The 10 June 2007 federal elections produced a fragmented result with CD&V/N-VA winning the most Flemish votes but unable to form a government for 194 days due to demands for state reform.

title: Fortis Bank Nationalization During Global Financial Crisis
reason: Fortis was partially nationalized on 28 September 2008 with Belgium, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg injecting 11.2 billion euros; the Belgian operations were subsequently sold to BNP Paribas.

title: Dexia Bank Requires Emergency Bailout
reason: On 30 September 2008, Franco-Belgian bank Dexia received a 6.4 billion euro emergency capital injection from the Belgian, French, and Luxembourg governments after toxic asset exposure and a liquidity crisis threatened its collapse.

title: Federal Elections Begin Record 541-Day Government Deadlock
reason: The 13 June 2010 elections produced a fragmented result with N-VA winning 27 seats and the Francophone Socialist Party 26, leading to a world-record 541-day government formation period.

title: Di Rupo Sworn In After World-Record Government Formation
reason: Elio Di Rupo was sworn in on 6 December 2011 after 541 days of negotiations, ending the longest government formation in modern democratic history; his six-party coalition made him Belgium's first Francophone socialist prime minister since 1974.

title: General Strike Against Austerity Pension Reforms
reason: Belgian unions called a general strike on 22 December 2011 against the Di Rupo government's 11.3 billion euro austerity package including pension age increases, paralyzing public transport, schools, and government services.

title: BHV Electoral District Split Resolves Decades-Old Dispute
reason: The Chamber of Representatives voted on 13 July 2012 (106 to 42) to split the Brussels-Halle-Vilvoorde electoral district, separating Flemish Brabant's Halle-Vilvoorde area from the Brussels-Capital Region for electoral purposes.

title: Sixth State Reform Devolves 20 Billion Euros in Powers
reason: The Butterfly Agreement (Vlinderakkoord) launched Belgium's sixth state reform transferring approximately 20 billion euros in annual competencies from the federal level to the Regions and Communities, the largest power transfer in Belgian federal history.

title: Charles Michel Forms Centre-Right Coalition with N-VA
reason: Charles Michel was sworn in on 11 October 2014 as the youngest Belgian prime minister since 1841, heading a coalition of MR, N-VA, Open Vld, and CD&V — the first time N-VA participated in a federal government.

title: NATO Wales Summit Increases Belgian Defense Commitments
reason: At the NATO Wales Summit (4-5 September 2014), all allies including Belgium pledged to move toward spending 2% of GDP on defense within a decade; Belgium's defense spending was among the lowest in the alliance at the time.

title: Molenbeek Linked to Paris Attacks Sparks Security Overhaul
reason: The November 2015 Paris attacks killing 130 people were traced to a jihadist cell operating from the Brussels commune of Molenbeek; Belgium raised its terror threat to maximum and locked down Brussels while hunting suspects.

title: Brussels Airport and Metro Bombings Kill 32 People
reason: On 22 March 2016, ISIS-linked suicide bombers struck Brussels Airport at Zaventem and the Maalbeek metro station killing 32 people and injuring over 300; the attackers belonged to the same cell responsible for the 2015 Paris attacks.

title: N-VA Exits Government Over UN Migration Pact Dispute
reason: N-VA withdrew from the governing coalition in December 2018 over Prime Minister Michel's decision to sign the UN Global Compact for Migration in Marrakech; Michel resigned on 18 December after parliament passed a motion of no confidence.

title: Youth Climate Strikes Mobilize Tens of Thousands Weekly
reason: From January 2019, Belgian students led by Anuna De Wever and Adélaïde Charlier organized weekly school climate strikes in Brussels drawing up to tens of thousands; Flemish Environment Minister Joke Schauvliege resigned after falsely claiming protests were orchestrated by intelligence services.

title: Fragmented Elections Produce Record Vlaams Belang Gains
reason: The 26 May 2019 federal elections saw Vlaams Belang triple its federal seats from 3 to 18, its best federal result ever, while producing extreme fragmentation that eventually required 493 days to form a new government.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Devastates Belgian Care Homes
reason: Belgium suffered one of the highest per-capita COVID-19 death rates in the EU, with over half of deaths (64% in the first wave) occurring in care homes; Prime Minister Sophie Wilmes led the caretaker government's pandemic response.

title: De Croo Vivaldi Coalition Formed After 493-Day Negotiations
reason: Alexander De Croo was sworn in as prime minister on 1 October 2020 (494 days after the 2019 elections) at the head of a seven-party Vivaldi coalition comprising liberals, socialists, greens, and CD&V, the second longest formation in Belgian history.

title: King Philippe Expresses Regrets for Colonial Past in Congo
reason: On 30 June 2020, the 60th anniversary of Congolese independence, King Philippe sent a letter to President Tshisekedi expressing his deepest regrets for the suffering and humiliation inflicted during Belgian colonial rule — unprecedented in Belgian royal history.

title: Catastrophic Floods Kill 39 in Wallonia
reason: Unprecedented rainfall between 12-15 July 2021 caused the Vesdre, Ourthe, Ambleve, and Meuse rivers to burst their banks, killing 39 people and causing an estimated 2.8 billion euros in damage across Wallonia.

title: Lumumba's Remains Returned to Congo in Colonial Reckoning
reason: On 20 June 2022, Belgium returned a gold tooth believed to be the only physical remains of Patrice Lumumba to his family in a ceremony at the Egmont Palace in Brussels; the tooth had been seized from the daughter of a Belgian police commissioner who participated in the disposal of Lumumba's body.

title: Colonial Reckoning Commission Fails to Approve Formal Apology
reason: Belgium's parliamentary colonial commission failed in late 2022 to achieve consensus on a formal apology to Congo, Rwanda, and Burundi, with liberal parties MR and Open VLD blocking the apology over fears of financial reparations claims.

title: Belgium Extends Two Nuclear Reactors Amid Energy Crisis
reason: On 18 March 2022, amid the energy crisis triggered by the Russia-Ukraine war, Prime Minister De Croo announced Belgium would extend the operation of Doel 4 and Tihange 3 by ten years beyond their planned 2025 closure.

title: Federal Elections Confirm Rightward Shift in Flanders
reason: The 9 June 2024 federal elections saw N-VA remain Belgium's largest party (24 federal seats) while Vlaams Belang won nearly one million votes and became the largest party in three of five Flemish provinces, confirming a structural rightward shift.

title: Bart De Wever Becomes First Flemish Nationalist Prime Minister
reason: N-VA leader Bart De Wever was sworn in on 3 February 2025 at the head of the five-party Arizona coalition (N-VA, CD&V, Vooruit, MR, and Les Engages) after more than eight months of negotiations following the June 2024 elections.

title: Belgium Reverses Nuclear Phase-Out With New Expansion Law
reason: The Belgian parliament voted 102 to 8 on 15 May 2025 to repeal the 2003 nuclear phase-out law, with Energy Minister Mathieu Bihet announcing plans to double nuclear capacity, marking a dramatic reversal of two decades of energy policy.
